name: @revheat/ui
//scripts: Named 'compile' NOT 'build' on purpose: pacote treats a 'build' (or prepare/install/prepack) script as a trigger to run `npm install` inside the git-dep clone, which pulls this package's devDeps and crashes arborist. dist/ is committed, so consumers never build. After editing src/, run `npm run compile` and commit dist/.
//verify: Run this before tagging a release. Every spec imports ../src/*, so a stale dist/ passes the whole suite green while shipping the OLD code to all four consumer apps — the exact drift the /icons export exists to end. This is the only thing that catches it, and it cannot be a prepare/prepack hook (see //scripts above).

scripts.check:dist: [ -z "$(git status --porcelain -- dist)" ] || { echo 'dist/ is stale, staged-but-uncommitted, or has untracked files. Run: npm run compile, then COMMIT dist/'; exit 1; }
scripts.check:client: [ "$(head -1 dist/react.js)" = '"use client";' ] || { echo 'dist/react.js lost its "use client" directive — both Next.js consumers fail to build without it'; exit 1; }; [ "$(head -1 dist/vue.js)" != '"use client";' ] || { echo 'dist/vue.js must not carry "use client" — it has no React import graph to gate'; exit 1; }; ! grep -q 'from "react' dist/vue.js || { echo 'dist/vue.js imports from react — that drags the whole React import graph into Vue-only consumers'; exit 1; }
scripts.verify: npm run compile && npm test && npm run check:client && npm run check:dist

//check:client: AppShell uses hooks (useState/useEffect/useId) and createPortal, and both React consumers mount it from an async Server Component. Without the directive on line 1 of dist/react.js their build fails outright with 'useState only works in a Client Component'. It was decorative through v1.3.0, when AppShell was hook-free; from v1.4.0 it is load-bearing, so it gets a gate.
//peerDependencies: react-dom is optional on purpose even though ./react imports createPortal from it. The Vue consumers (Call Analyzer) import only ./icons and ./catalog, so their bundler never resolves react-dom and marking it required would only produce a peer warning on an install that is completely fine. Any app importing ./react is a React DOM app and already has it. `vue` is optional for the same reason: a React-only consumer never resolves it, and a required peer would only produce a spurious install warning.
